description: A four-channel oscilloscope with an automatic time base, a trigger section, statistics, and X-Y plotting

params.text: Moves that channel's trace up or down the screen, by up to five divisions either way
Sets the time across one division, from 10µs to 1 second
Sets how long the trigger is held off after firing, from 100µs to 10 seconds
Sets the voltage the trigger fires at, from -10V to 10V
Chooses which channel the trigger is taken from, A, B, C, D or the external trigger jack
Chooses the trigger mode: Auto sweeps whether or not a trigger arrives, Norm sweeps only on a trigger, Single sweeps once and stops, and X-Y plots one channel against another instead of against time
Chooses whether the trigger fires on a rising or a falling edge
Freezes the display at the end of the sweep now being drawn, or at once in X-Y mode; pressing it again releases the freeze
Turns the automatic time base on and off; with it on the time per division is set from the frequency measured on the trigger channel
Steps the statistics readout through three settings: off, the trigger channel alone, and every channel
Sets that channel's volts per division, in thirteen steps from 20V down to 5mV, the first of which switches the channel off
Switches that channel between the audio drawing, which fills each pixel column with the highest and lowest sample in it, and the CV drawing, which joins the samples with a line

inputs.text: A signal to trigger from, used when the source is set to the external trigger

outputs.text: A 10V pulse at every trigger the module finds, sent whether or not the display is frozen and whatever the holdoff is set to

notes: the display is drawn by the module rather than built from Rack widgets, so nothing on it can be clicked for help; it is 20 divisions across and 8 down.
the maker registered the trigger output with the call that names an input, so the channel A input jack shows the trigger output's description and the trigger output shows no name.
changing the trigger source, the trigger mode or the edge clears the measured frequency and cancels any holdoff already running.
a polyphonic cable into a channel can show all sixteen of its channels at once; which of them are drawn, and which one the trigger is taken from, are set on the menu.
menu: Show grid — draws the division grid behind the traces
Show baselines — draws a line across the screen at each channel's zero level
Show centerline — draws a line across the middle of the screen
Auto-time periods 1 — fits one cycle of the measured wave across the screen when the automatic time base is on
Auto-time periods 3 — fits three cycles of the measured wave across the screen when the automatic time base is on, which is where the module starts
Auto-time periods 10 — fits ten cycles of the measured wave across the screen when the automatic time base is on
Auto-time periods 25 — fits twenty-five cycles of the measured wave across the screen when the automatic time base is on
Auto-time periods 50 — fits fifty cycles of the measured wave across the screen when the automatic time base is on
AC Coupling (Block DC) — opens a line per channel, each reading DC or AC; on AC a 0.1Hz filter takes the offset out of that channel before it is drawn
Polyphony — opens a line per channel, each holding View Channels, which ticks which of the sixteen polyphonic channels are drawn, and Trigger Source, which picks one of them
X-Y Plot Routing — opens Plot 1 and Plot 2, each with an X-Axis Source and a Y-Axis Source chosen from Channel A to Channel D or Off
